target.name: Unone AI-native Audit
target.scope: Same-agent retest of Scout 0.3.0 through its public standalone CLI: README/help → recommend → describe(init/evaluate) → init → complete report → evaluate. Execution evidence is supplemented by probe.capture-004; registry writes and host/MCP/UI integrations are outside this trial.
target.revision: Current reviewed working tree; selected-file hashes match probe.capture-004 and sourceChanged is false.
target.environment: Windows x64, Node.js v24.14.1, standalone local CLI; no Unone host, MCP server, GUI, or external provider.

limitations: This is a same-agent retest with prior task context; the fresh execution began from README/help and used only public CLI/docs plus the supplied capture.
One local Windows x64 / Node.js v24.14.1 CLI environment; no host, MCP transport, GUI, other OS/device, or cross-device flow was exercised.

probe.capture-004's evaluation step uses a synthetic all-unverified report to show evaluator observability; it explicitly is not a Scout score. The completed report score is produced by this retest's stdin evaluation.
No src/ or test/ file contents were inspected. The capture's subject hashes are included to bind this report to the reviewed snapshot.

checks.answer: Scout is clearly identified as an audit plugin for helping unfamiliar AI discover, use, understand, and repair tools. The exact README task query now recommends ai_native.init first; its summary and nextAction both identify it as the start of a new assessment.
checks.reason: The public purpose and boundaries are explicit, and the fresh English query led directly to the right first operation without conflicting ranking.
checks.nextAction: Keep the new-assessment phrase and start instruction aligned across README examples and recommend output.

checks.answer: The README and public catalog/describe expose the assessment workflow, Node.js requirement, stdin/in-memory report input, deterministic keyword-search limitation, and registration write boundary. The operation descriptions are compact until selected.
checks.reason: The available workflow and constraints are discoverable for this task. The search is explicitly limited to supplied metadata and I did not exercise registry/history operations.
checks.nextAction: Continue adding representative English and Chinese paraphrases to discovery probes while preserving the declared keyword-search limitation.

checks.answer: I completed the requested workflow using public entrypoints: help, recommend, describe init, init, describe evaluate, catalog, prepare the report, and evaluate it from stdin. Init returned ten checks without file-writing effects; evaluate accepts the completed report from stdin.
checks.reason: The chosen path works end to end from the documented discovery flow. The supplied probe also captures a successful in-memory evaluate call, while the direct retest evaluated this report.
checks.nextAction: Preserve the recommend → describe → init → evaluate path and keep the in-memory/stdin route visible in the selected evaluate contract.

checks.answer: The report contract retains target ID/name/surface/scope/version/revision/environment, trial metadata, selected subject hashes, evidence references, per-check answers, and next actions/issues. The README clarifies the difference between package release and per-operation contract version.
checks.reason: The report schema provides the context needed for this self-audit and ties claims to the selected source/document snapshot.
checks.nextAction: Keep the versionScope description visible whenever a contract version appears outside the describe response.

checks.answer: The evaluator returns an index, possible range, coverage, gate, blockers, unverified-critical checks, and per-dimension accepted scores. capture-004 demonstrates that an all-unverified report returns index null and insufficient_evidence instead of inventing a score; this retest also obtained an output for the completed report.
checks.reason: Results and failure/insufficient-evidence states are machine-readable. The capture's scoring case is intentionally synthetic and does not certify Scout; the final completed-report output is from this direct retest.
checks.nextAction: Keep evaluator output fields stable and add a reviewed capture for a fully evidenced report when a persisted scored-run artifact is needed.

checks.answer: A typoed operation returns DISCOVERY_OPERATION_UNKNOWN with actual/expected values and a likely-operation suggestion; the supplied capture retries the suggested ai_native.evaluate describe successfully. A traversal input returns AUDIT_PATH_OUTSIDE_ROOT and a concrete in-root path correction.
checks.reason: Both negative cases are specific and actionable, and the typo repair was followed by a successful public describe.
checks.nextAction: Retain the exact likely-operation and root-boundary diagnostics; capture completed-report field-error repair when expanding probe coverage.

checks.answer: The typo path can be repaired through the suggested describe call and the smoke checks stale-contract rejection. Lost host replies, interrupted calls, and safe retry of append-only registration were not exercised.
checks.reason: Read-only discovery recovery is demonstrated, but broader stateful retry/idempotency behavior remains unverified and register was out of scope.
checks.nextAction: Add a public stale-hash re-describe-and-retry case and document handling of an uncertain registry append without duplicating it.

checks.answer: Init/evaluate are read-only, registration requires trusted host opt-in, and a captured traversal attempt is rejected with AUDIT_PATH_OUTSIDE_ROOT. The probe is local and uses no external provider or user project data.
checks.reason: The key evidence-root boundary was exercised and the write boundary is explicit. Registration itself was not called, as required by the task scope.
checks.nextAction: Keep the host-level test that verifies registry writes stay disabled without trusted opt-in.

checks.answer: CLI telemetry gives plugin wall time and explicitly says it is not target performance. No memory, CPU, provider cost, or target-service latency was measured, and no GPU value is fabricated.
checks.reason: The tool reports its own local timing honestly, but this trial only supports a narrow latency view.
checks.nextAction: Keep the current distinction and expose resource/cost metrics only where the host can measure them reliably.

checks.answer: capture-004 records the command, Node/platform, output, exit codes, probe hash, exact 18-file subject hashes, and sourceChanged=false. README and describe clearly distinguish plugin release from per-operation contract versions, and the completed report can be re-evaluated from the saved report file.
checks.reason: The source snapshot and environment are traceable and version semantics are no longer ambiguous. The capture's evaluate fixture is synthetic, so the completed report's score is not captured as a separate replay artifact.
checks.nextAction: Save a reviewed capture of a fully evidenced report if an independently replayable scored-run record is required.
